Fed Signals Rate Cut in June Meeting

The Federal Reserve has indicated it may cut interest rates at its June meeting, citing cooling inflation and a softening labor market. Chair Jerome Powell noted that while progress on inflation has been made, the committee remains data-dependent.

Markets reacted positively to the news, with the S&P 500 rising 1.2% in afternoon trading. Bond yields fell as traders priced in a higher probability of a cut.

Economists are divided on the timing. Goldman Sachs expects a quarter-point cut in June, while Morgan Stanley believes the Fed will wait until September for more data.

The decision will hinge on the May CPI report, due out two weeks before the meeting. Core inflation is expected to remain sticky around 3.2%.
